title: Networking and Connector Activity dashboards: traffic, data-center and connector maps, discovered devices, Cloud and Branch Connector activity

prose.text: {{networking-time-range}} The time range is said to apply to all data in the dashboard, yet Devices Discovered covers the most recent 24 hours, and the User Devices widget's percentage is undefined {{gap:networking-details}}.

prose.label: Connector Activity.
prose.text: {{connector-activity-filters}} {{connector-activity-rings}} {{connector-activity-table}} The Cloud and Branch Connector console counterpart is [[cloud-connector.insights.dashboard]], and its Connectors table columns are in [[cloud-connector.insights.connector-status]]. The Connector Activity page states no time range {{gap:connector-activity-range}}.

networking-time-range.statement: The Networking dashboard provides information about traffic, data centers and devices; its time range runs between 1 Day and 90 Days, applies to all data within the dashboard, and defaults to 14 Days.

quotes: The Networking dashboard provides information about traffic, data centers, and devices in your organization.
between 1 Day and 90 Days in which to view data
The selected period applies to all data within the dashboard.
The default time range is 14 Days.

networking-traffic.statement: Traffic in my Organization charts the number of transactions and the overall traffic volume with their percentage change, and traffic for Road Warrior (totally remote) versus In-Office users, toggled between Internet and Private application traffic; further widgets show the road-warrior versus in-office distribution and the top locations sending traffic through Zscaler.

quotes: Traffic in my Organization
This widget shows three line graphs:
Number of transactions and percentage change for the selected time period
Overall traffic volume and percentage change for the selected time period
Traffic volume in your network, for Road Warrior, or totally remote users (indicated by the blue line) and In-Office users (indicated by the green line).
Click Internet or Private to toggle between viewing internet or private application traffic.
a circle graph that shows the distribution of traffic between road warriors and in-office users in your organization
This bar chart shows the top locations that are sending traffic through Zscaler.

networking-map.statement: The map has Data Centers (dot size shows traffic flowing through the location), App Connectors (dot size shows connectors in use) and Cloud & Branch Connectors tabs (dot size shows connectors in use); clicking a location shows the connector type, health status, location and traffic, boxes limit the view to Cloud Connectors or Branch Connectors, and View Connector Activity opens the Connector Activity dashboard.

quotes: On the Data Centers tab, the relative size of the dot indicates how much traffic is flowing through the location.
On the App Connectors tab, the relative size of the dot indicates how many connectors are in use at that location.
On the Cloud & Branch Connectors tab, the relative size of the dot indicates how many connectors are in use at that location.
Click a location to see the type of connector, its health status, location, and traffic.
Check the boxes to view only Cloud Connectors or Branch Connectors.
Click View Connector Activity to open the Connector Activity Dashboard.

networking-devices.statement: Device widgets show the total number of devices discovered with a bar graph of operating system distribution, and the breakdown of devices (such as smartphones, computers, printers and peripherals, and IoT devices) discovered in the most recent 24 hours.

quotes: This widget shows the total number of devices that have been discovered in your organization
A bar graph shows the distribution of operating systems for all the devices in your organization.
This widget shows the breakdown of devices, such as smartphones, computers, printers and peripherals, and IOT devices, that have been discovered in your organization in the most recent 24 hours.

connector-activity-filters.statement: The Connector Activity dashboard toggles between Cloud Connectors and Branch Connectors and filters, each able to include or exclude options, by Geolocation, Status (Active or Inactive), Connector Type (Physical or Virtual Branch Connector) and Connector Location.

quotes: The Connector Activity dashboard provides an overview of Cloud Connector and Branch Connector activity in your organization.
Click Cloud Connectors or Branch Connectors to toggle between viewing activity for each type of connector.
Each filter allows you to include or exclude individual options.
Geolocation: The geographic area where the Cloud Connector or Branch Connector is located.
Status: The status of the Cloud Connector or Branch Connector (i.e., Active or Inactive).
Connector Type: The type of Branch Connector (i.e., Physical or Virtual).
Connector Location: The named location of a Cloud Connector or Branch Connector.

connector-activity-rings.statement: The Traffic Volume Across Service and Session Across Service ring charts split the throughput and session counts of the provisioned and deployed connectors into Internet (through the Internet & SaaS cloud), Private (through the Private Applications cloud), Direct (forwarded directly) and Log & Control (through the Log and Control gateway).

quotes: Traffic Volume Across Service
Session Across Service
Internet: The session count data forwarded through the Internet & SaaS cloud.
Private: The session count data forwarded through the Private Applications cloud.
Direct: The session count data forwarded directly.
Log & Control: The session count data forwarded through the Log and Control gateway.
This ring chart shows the throughput of the traffic flowing through the Cloud Connectors or Branch Connectors that are provisioned and deployed in your cloud or branch accounts.
Internet: The throughput forwarded through the Internet & SaaS cloud.
Private: The throughput forwarded through the Private Applications cloud.
Direct: The throughput forwarded directly.
Log & Control: The throughput forwarded through the Log and Control gateway.
This ring chart shows the session count data for the Cloud Connectors or Branch Connectors

connector-activity-table.statement: The Connectors table gives, among its columns, Group, Autoscaling (True or False), Status (Active or Inactive), HA Status (Branch Connector), VM Size (Cloud Connector, Small or Medium) and Model (for a physical Branch Connector the hardware device, for example ZT800; Virtual for a virtual connector); the same details are also available under Infrastructure > Connectors > Cloud > Cloud Connector Monitoring and Infrastructure > Connectors > Edge > Branch Connector Monitoring.

quotes: Group: The group to which the Cloud Connector or Branch Connector is assigned.
Autoscaling: The status of autoscaling (i.e., True or False).
Status: The status of this Cloud Connector or Branch Connector (i.e., Active or Inactive).
HA Status: The high availability status of the Branch Connector.
VM Size: The size of the virtual machine for a Cloud Connector (i.e., Small or Medium).
Model: For a physical Branch Connector, the type of hardware device (e.g., ZT800); Virtual for a virtual connector.
You can also view these details by going to Infrastructure > Connectors > Cloud > Cloud Connector Monitoring.
You can also view these details by going to Infrastructure > Connectors > Edge > Branch Connector Monitoring.

networking-details.title: Networking dashboard widget definitions
networking-details.detail: The User Devices widget's percentage time for the selected time period is undefined. Devices Discovered covers the most recent 24 hours while the page says the selected period applies to all data within the dashboard; both are recorded and neither is resolved. The App Connectors tab's click-through text is truncated on the page.

connector-activity-range.title: Connector Activity dashboard time range
connector-activity-range.detail: The Connector Activity page states no time range.
